extracted.intended_audience: researchers and clinicians in aging/geroscience considering submission to the Aging-US journal
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for authors preparing manuscripts for Aging-US, a peer-reviewed journal focused on biological mechanisms of aging and translational interventions to extend healthspan. Emphasizes work that links fundamental biology to clinical application, including innovative technologies, novel models, and early-phase clinical trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancing understanding of biological mechanisms of aging
rubrics_metrics.description: Aging-US is dedicated to advancing our understanding of the biological mechanisms that drive aging and the development of age-related diseases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should uncover cellular, molecular, and systemic processes underlying aging and provide insights that can inform interventions; the journal serves as a platform for research that deepens mechanistic knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality research
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal aims to serve as a platform for high-quality research that uncovers the cellular, molecular, and systemic processes underlying aging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not exhaustively defined on this page, 'high-quality' work is implied to include rigorous methodology, clear reporting, and contribution to the field; quality is maintained through rigorous and constructive peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of interventions that target the aging process
rubrics_metrics.description: The treatment of age-related diseases through interventions that target the aging process itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that propose, evaluate, or validate interventions aimed at modifying aging mechanisms (rather than only treating individual diseases) are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of anti-aging therapies via functional and disease endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: The validation of anti-aging therapies by demonstrating their impact on functional decline and disease onset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should provide evidence that interventions meaningfully affect functional outcomes and/or delay or prevent disease onset; mechanistic and translational evidence that links intervention to healthspan benefit is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of preventative strategies targeting key aging mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: The development of preventative strategies that delay or mitigate age-associated pathologies by modulating key aging mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work describing preventive approaches and showing modulation of recognized aging mechanisms (with potential to delay pathology) fits the journal's aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcomes innovative technologies, novel model systems, and early-phase clinical trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Aging-US actively welcomes studies that utilize innovative technologies, novel model systems, and early-phase clinical trials to accelerate the translation of aging research into meaningful interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should highlight novel methods, models, or early clinical data that facilitate translation from basic biology to interventions; emphasis on accelerating clinical relevance and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bridge fundamental biology with clinical application (healthspan focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: By bridging fundamental biology with clinical application, the journal supports a paradigm shift from disease treatment to healthspan preservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts that make clear connections between mechanistic findings and potential clinical application—especially those reframing goals toward preserving healthspan—are aligned with the journal's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous and constructive peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigorous and constructive peer review is essential to scientific progress; reviewers' careful evaluations maintain the scientific quality, integrity, and credibility of the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should expect and prepare for critical, constructive peer review. Clear, reproducible reporting and transparent methods will facilitate favorable evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility and archiving expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Aging-US is archived and indexed in databases such as PubMed/Medline, PubMed Central, Web of Science (noting a recent WOS Core Collection discontinuation under appeal), Scopus, Biological Abstracts, BIOSIS Previews, EMBASE, Dimensions, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can expect their work to be discoverable across major bibliographic and archival services; note the journal's ongoing interactions with indexing services (e.g., Web of Science) which may affect indexing status.
